summary: This paper systematically studies measurement-induced state transitions (MIST) in fluxonium qubits across the experimentally explored parameter space using branch analysis over $2 	imes 10^6$ parameter combinations, finding that lighter fluxoniums ($E_J/E_L 	o 3$–$6$) are less susceptible to MIST than heavier ones. The authors identify three physical mechanisms responsible for this difference: lower density of multi-photon resonances, smaller required coupling for a target dispersive shift $ ar{ ar{ ar{ ar{ ar{}}}}}$, and more harmonic charge operator structure in light fluxoniums.
motivation: Readout remains the slowest and lowest-fidelity operation in superconducting quantum processors, and while MIST has been extensively characterized for transmons, a systematic study of this effect across the full fluxonium parameter landscape is lacking despite fluxoniums demonstrating $T_1 \gtrsim 1$ ms and gate fidelities exceeding 99.9%, making them a serious alternative for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The authors performed branch analysis on the fluxonium-resonator Hamiltonian with capacitive coupling, extracting critical photon numbers $n_{\text{crit}}$ as the resonator photon number at which average fluxonium population reaches $\langle \hat{N}_f \rangle = 2$ (ground) or $3$ (excited); they also validated predictions with time-dependent master equation simulations and extended analysis to include superinductor array modes via Floquet branch analysis.
result: Light fluxoniums achieve average critical photon numbers $\bar{n}_{\text{crit}} > 200$ over 700 MHz bandwidth (compared to $\bar{n}_{\text{crit}} \approx 10$–$30$ for heavy variants); time-dependent simulations demonstrate readout fidelity of $1 - \epsilon = 99.97\%$ at $\tau \sim 100$ ns integration time for optimal parameters, though residual leakage to states $|3_f\rangle$ and $|5_f\rangle$ remains at $\sim 0.3$–$0.6\%$ even without MIST-driven transitions.
